grahas.title: The nine grahas

method.title: How it is calculated
method.p1: The Sun and planets come from Keplerian orbital elements with the main Jupiter–Saturn perturbations. The Moon uses the 60-term lunar series from Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms. Rahu is the mean lunar node. Positions are converted to sidereal with the Lahiri ayanamsa, and the Lagna is solved from local sidereal time and latitude.
method.p2: Checked against the Swiss Ephemeris on 3,000 dates from 1900 to 2100: Moon within about 1′, Lagna within 1′, other grahas within 3½′. Houses are whole-sign. Yogas and doshas follow the rules shown on each card; traditions differ on cancellations.

static.featTitle: A complete Vedic birth chart, free
static.featLede: Grahavani calculates your chart from first principles, then reads it with classical Jyotish rules.

features.p: Sidereal degrees of all nine grahas, checked against the Swiss Ephemeris.
In North Indian or South Indian style.
Raj yoga, Gajakesari, Mangal dosha, Kaal Sarp, Sade Sati and more, each with the rule shown.
Mahadasha and antardasha dates for 100 years, with the running period highlighted.
Tithi, vara, nakshatra, yoga, karana, sunrise and sunset.
All twelve houses with lords, occupants and bindu strength.
Gochar from your Moon sign, marked favourable or unfavourable.
Every chart you make is saved to your account. Only you can see it.

p: A Janma Kundali (birth chart) is a map of the sky at the exact moment and place of your birth. It shows the Lagna (the sign rising in the east), the twelve bhavas (houses) and the positions of the nine grahas in the twelve rashis and twenty-seven nakshatras.
Jyotish reads this map to understand temperament, strengths and challenges, and uses the Vimshottari dasha system to time the main periods of life.

Your birth time is converted to Universal Time using the time zone history of your birth place. The positions of the Sun, Moon and planets are then computed from orbital mathematics and converted to the sidereal zodiac with the Lahiri ayanamsa, the standard used by the Government of India's calendar.
The Lagna is solved from local sidereal time and your latitude. Yogas, doshas and strengths are then checked with stated classical rules, so you can see why each result appears.

static.faqLede: Answers to common questions about Kundali and how this site works.

faq.a: A Kundali, or Janma Kundali, is a Vedic birth chart: the positions of the Sun, Moon, planets, Rahu and Ketu at the moment of your birth, arranged in twelve houses from the Lagna (ascendant). It is the basis of all Jyotish readings.

faq.q: What details do I need to make my Kundali?
faq.a: Your date of birth, exact time of birth and place of birth. The place gives latitude, longitude and time zone, which are needed to calculate the Lagna and houses correctly.

faq.q: What if I don't know my exact birth time?
faq.a: Planet signs and most nakshatras will still be correct, because they change slowly. The Lagna changes about every two hours and the Lagna degree about every four minutes, so house positions and dasha dates depend on an accurate time.

Planet positions are calculated with astronomical formulas and were tested against the Swiss Ephemeris for 1900 to 2100. The Moon and Lagna agree within about one arc-minute, and the other planets within about three and a half arc-minutes.
It uses the Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsa, the standard adopted by the Indian Calendar Reform Committee and used by most Indian astrologers and panchangs.

Mangal dosha is present when Mars sits in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house. Grahavani checks it from the Lagna, the Moon and Venus. Many traditions also apply cancellation rules, so discuss important decisions with an astrologer.

Vimshottari is a 120-year cycle of planetary periods. Your starting period depends on the nakshatra of the Moon at birth. Each mahadasha is divided into nine antardashas, and Grahavani lists the dates for 100 years.

faq.q: Why do I need to log in, and is my data private?
faq.a: Your first Kundali is free with no account. To make more Kundalis, create a free account. It takes a few seconds and needs no email verification. Each chart is saved to your account so you can open it later, with row-level security so only you can read it.

footer.text: Positions are computed from orbital mathematics with Lahiri ayanamsa. Readings follow classical rules and are a guide, not a certainty.

varga.title: Divisional charts (Vargas)
varga.lede: Each varga divides every sign into equal parts to look at one area of life in detail.

D2.name: Hora
D2.about: Hora splits each sign in two (Sun and Moon halves). It shows how wealth is earned and kept.

D3.name: Drekkana
D3.about: Drekkana divides each sign into three. It is read for siblings, courage and initiative.

D4.name: Chaturthamsha
D4.about: Chaturthamsha divides each sign into four. It is read for home, land, vehicles and fixed assets.

D7.name: Saptamsha
D7.about: Saptamsha divides each sign into seven. It is read for children and progeny.

D10.name: Dashamsha
D10.about: Dashamsha divides each sign into ten. It is the main chart for career, status and achievements.

D12.name: Dwadashamsha
D12.about: Dwadashamsha divides each sign into twelve. It is read for parents and ancestry.

rf.chandrashtama: Chandrashtama: Moon in the 8th — keep the day light, avoid big decisions.
rf.note: Daily Rashifal is a general reading for everyone with the same Moon sign. Your own Kundali, dasha and transits give a far more personal picture.
moon: Moon in your own sign: you feel more like yourself — good for health, comfort and personal plans.
Moon in the 2nd: money and family matters need attention; watch spending and words.
Moon in the 3rd: courage and energy rise — good for short trips, calls and effort.
Moon in the 4th: home and mother are in focus; mood can swing, so keep things calm.
Moon in the 5th: creativity and learning flow, but avoid speculation and rash choices.
Moon in the 6th: you overcome obstacles and finish pending work — a productive day.
Moon in the 7th: partnerships, meetings and travel go well; good for teamwork.
Moon in the 8th: a sensitive day — rest, avoid risks, arguments and big decisions.
Moon in the 9th: luck is mixed; spend time on study, prayer and elders' advice.
Moon in the 10th: work moves forward and you get noticed — good for important tasks.
Moon in the 11th: gains, good news and support from friends — one of the best days.
Moon in the 12th: expenses and tiredness rise; keep it simple and get some rest.

mt.title: Kundali Matching
mt.lede: Ashtakoot matching compares the Moon nakshatras of two people across eight factors, for a total of 36 points, and checks Mangal dosha for both.
mt.lockNote: Kundali matching is free for members. Log in or create an account in seconds to see the result.

vt.excellent: 33 or more points: a very strong traditional match.
vt.good: 25–32 points: a good match by the traditional standard.
vt.average: 18–24 points: acceptable; look at the individual kootas and both full charts.
vt.low: Below 18 points: traditionally not recommended without a detailed reading of both charts.

m.both: Both are Manglik, so the dosha is traditionally considered balanced.
m.one: Only one is Manglik. Traditionally this needs checking for cancellations in both charts before deciding.
m.none: Neither is Manglik, so there is no Mangal dosha concern.

mt.disclaimer: Guna Milan is one traditional input. A full compatibility reading also looks at both Kundalis, dashas and the 7th house.

kt.cancelled: Dosha cancelled: the Moon-sign lords are friends or the same.

varna.name: Varna
varna.rule: 1 point if the boy's varna is equal to or higher than the girl's.

vashya.name: Vashya
vashya.rule: Up to 2 points, by how the two Moon-sign groups relate.

tara.name: Tara
tara.rule: Count nakshatras each way and divide by 9; remainders 3, 5 and 7 are unlucky. 1.5 points per direction.

yoni.name: Yoni
yoni.rule: Up to 4 points by the animal symbol of each nakshatra; natural enemies score 0.

maitri.name: Graha Maitri
maitri.rule: Up to 5 points by the friendship of the two Moon-sign lords.

gana.name: Gana
gana.rule: Up to 6 points; Deva, Manushya and Rakshasa natures are compared.

bhakoot.name: Bhakoot
bhakoot.rule: 7 points unless the Moon signs are 2/12, 5/9 or 6/8 from each other.

nadi.name: Nadi
nadi.rule: 8 points if the Nadis differ; the same Nadi scores 0 (Nadi dosha).

p: Panchang means "five limbs". Every day is described by its tithi (lunar day), vara (weekday), nakshatra (Moon's star), yoga (Sun–Moon combination) and karana (half tithi). Together they are used to choose good times for work, travel, ceremonies and fasting.

Sunrise and sunset are computed for the city you choose. Each element's end time is found by solving for the exact moment the Moon and Sun reach the next boundary. Rahu Kaal, Yamaganda and Gulika are one-eighth parts of the daytime, and Choghadiya splits day and night into eight parts each.

Hindu festivals follow the lunar calendar. A festival is kept on the day its tithi is present at the right time — sunrise for most, midday for Ram Navami, evening for Diwali and midnight for Janmashtami and Shivaratri. Because these moments depend on your location, dates can differ by a day between cities and from printed calendars.

Months here are named in the Amanta system (month ends at new moon), used in Gujarat, Maharashtra and South India. In North India the Purnimanta system ends the month at full moon, so the month name for Krishna paksha dates is one month ahead; the festival dates themselves are the same.

Each sign's reading counts where the nine grahas are today from that Moon sign and applies the classical gochar (transit) rules: for example Jupiter is favourable in the 2nd, 5th, 7th, 9th and 11th, and Saturn in the 3rd, 6th and 11th. The Moon's house sets the mood of the day.
Vedic astrology reads the daily horoscope from your Moon sign (Rashi), not the western Sun sign. Make your free Kundali to find your Rashi — the site then highlights it here automatically.

Ashtakoot compares the two Moon nakshatras across eight kootas: Varna, Vashya, Tara, Yoni, Graha Maitri, Gana, Bhakoot and Nadi. Their points add up to 36. Traditionally 18 or more is acceptable and 25 or more is good.

Nadi and Bhakoot carry the most points, and a zero in either is called a dosha. Classical texts list cancellations, such as the Moon-sign lords being friends. Mangal dosha is checked from the Lagna, Moon and Venus for both people.

Each nakshatra has four padas, and each pada has a sacred first syllable (Akshar). Naming the child with that syllable is the traditional Namkaran practice. The names here start with your child's syllables; pick a pada to narrow the list.

The name number is the sum of the letters in the Chaldean system, reduced to one digit. Moolank comes from the day of birth and Bhagyank from the full date. A name whose number is friendly with these is marked lucky.

A muhurta is chosen from the tithi, nakshatra, weekday, yoga and karana. Each purpose has its own favourable stars and lunar days — for example Rohini, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta and Revati for marriage. Harsh yogas, Vishti karana and Rahu Kaal are avoided.

Marriage and griha pravesh are traditionally not held during Chaturmas, Kharmas (Sun in Dhanu or Meena), Adhika maas, Pitru Paksha, Holashtak, or while Jupiter or Venus is combust. Add your own Kundali to also skip days with bad Tara bala or Chandrashtama.

Birth details you enter (name, date, time and place) are used to calculate your Kundali. If you create an account, we store your email, the Kundalis you make and a history of your entries so you can open them again.
Without an account, your history stays only in your own browser. A small cookie remembers that this browser has used its free Kundali.

Your data is used only to show your charts and history. We do not sell it or share it with advertisers. Share links show a chart only to people you give the link to, and you can turn a link off at any time.
Accounts and saved charts are stored with Supabase with row-level security, so each account can read only its own data. Pages are served by Vercel, which also records anonymous visit statistics.
You can delete any saved Kundali or history entry from your account at any time. To delete your account completely, contact us from your registered email.
Grahavani is a free tool for calculating Vedic astrology charts and related information. You may use it for personal purposes. Do not misuse the service or try to access other people's data.
Readings follow classical rules and are for guidance and interest only. They are not medical, legal, financial or psychological advice, and important decisions should not be based on them alone.

Positions are calculated mathematically and checked against standard ephemerides, but results depend on the accuracy of the birth details entered. Festival dates can differ by a day from other calendars because of location and tradition.
You are responsible for keeping your password safe. We may suspend accounts that abuse the service. These terms may be updated; the date at the top shows the latest version.

lp.indexLede: What each of the nine grahas does in each of the twelve houses, and the nature of all twelve Lagnas — written from classical principles.
lp.phTitle: {g} in the {n} House – Effects in Vedic Astrology | Grahavani
lp.phDesc: Effects of {g} in the {n} house of the Kundali: what it means for {m}, when it is strong or weak, and its transit results.
lp.intro: {g} is the karaka (significator) of {kk}. The {n} house, called {hn} Bhava, shows {m}. When {g} sits here, these matters take on its colour.

ben: A benefic in the Lagna is a blessing: it gives a pleasant nature, good health and a likeable personality, and protects the whole chart.
In the 2nd house a benefic supports savings, a sweet and truthful way of speaking, and harmony in the family.
In the 3rd house a benefic makes one gentle in effort; it favours communication, writing and good relations with siblings, though drive may be soft.
In the 4th house a benefic brings a comfortable home, vehicles, a caring mother and peace of mind.
In the 5th house a benefic is excellent for intelligence, learning, creativity and children.
In the 6th house a benefic is somewhat weakened; it helps one serve others and settle disputes kindly, but can bring small health or debt matters.
In the 7th house a benefic supports a good spouse, happy partnerships and success in dealing with the public.
In the 8th house a benefic protects longevity and brings interest in research and hidden subjects, though its outward results are reduced.
In the 9th house a benefic is very fortunate: it brings luck, faith, higher learning and support from father and teachers.
In the 10th house a benefic brings respect, ethical work and a good name in one's career.
In the 11th house every graha gives gains; a benefic here brings steady income and helpful friends.
In the 12th house a benefic turns spending toward good causes and supports sleep, spiritual life and foreign connections.
mal: A malefic in the Lagna gives strength of will and drive, but can make one impatient or harsh and needs care for health.
In the 2nd house a malefic can make speech sharp and finances uneven, and calls for care in family relations.
In the 3rd house a malefic is at its best: it gives courage, initiative and the will to win through effort.
In the 4th house a malefic can disturb peace at home or with property, and asks one to build inner calm.
In the 5th house a malefic can delay children or unsettle the mind, while giving a sharp, practical intelligence.
In the 6th house a malefic is welcome: it defeats enemies, clears debts and gives the stamina to compete.
In the 7th house a malefic can bring friction or delay in marriage and partnerships, and calls for patience with others.
In the 8th house a malefic can bring sudden events and hidden worries, yet also resilience and depth.
In the 9th house a malefic can test faith or relations with father and teachers, and makes one follow one's own path.
In the 10th house a malefic gives ambition, authority and hard-won success in career.
In the 11th house a malefic is strong: it brings gains, fulfilment of desires and influential contacts.
In the 12th house a malefic can raise expenses, losses or sleep trouble, but also helps detachment and work abroad.

cls.kendra: The {n} house is a kendra (angular house), a pillar of the chart, so a graha here shows its results openly and strongly.
cls.trikona: The {n} house is a trikona (trine), one of the houses of fortune, which improves whatever graha sits here.
cls.dusthana: The {n} house is a dusthana (house of difficulty), so results here come through challenges and need conscious handling.
cls.upachaya: The {n} house is an upachaya (house of growth): results improve steadily with time and effort.
cls.maraka: The {n} house is a maraka (sensitive) house as well as a house of resources, so results depend strongly on the graha's dignity.

lp.digbala: {g} gains directional strength (Dig Bala) in the {n} house, which noticeably strengthens it here.
lp.digWeak: The {n} house is opposite to where {g} gets directional strength, so it loses some power here.
lp.strong: {g} gives its best results here when it is exalted in {ex}, in its own sign ({own}) or in a friendly sign, and when it is not combust.
lp.strongNode: {g} is a shadow graha and gives the results of the sign lord and conjunct grahas; it is considered strong in {ex}.
lp.weak: Results are weaker if {g} is debilitated in {deb}, combust, or afflicted by malefics.
lp.weakSun: Results are weaker if the Sun is debilitated in {deb} or afflicted by Saturn or Rahu.
lp.gocharFav: When {g} transits the {n} house counted from your Moon sign, the period is traditionally favourable.
lp.gocharUnfav: When {g} transits the {n} house counted from your Moon sign, the period traditionally needs more care.
lp.cta: See which house {g} occupies in your own chart, with its strength and dignity.
lp.disclaimer: A single placement is never read alone: sign, aspects, conjunctions, dasha and the whole chart change the outcome.

lp.lgMal: {list} rule the 3rd, 6th or 11th house and tend to bring effort and obstacles.

manglik.name: Mangal Dosha
manglik.what: Mars in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house from the Lagna or Moon. Tradition links it to friction and delay in marriage.
do: Recite the Hanuman Chalisa on Tuesdays and offer sindoor to Hanumanji.
Fast on Tuesdays and donate red lentils (masoor) and jaggery.
Chant “Om Angarakaya Namah” 108 times a day.
Match charts carefully before marriage — Mangal dosha in both charts balances out.

kaalsarp.name: Kaal Sarp Yoga
kaalsarp.what: All seven grahas sit on one side of the Rahu–Ketu axis.
do: Chant the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra 108 times a day.
Offer milk and water on the Shivling on Mondays, especially in Shravan.
Have a Kaal Sarp shanti puja done once at a temple such as Trimbakeshwar or Ujjain.
Feed birds and serve snakes' shrines (Nag devta) on Nag Panchami.

sadesati.name: Sade Sati
sadesati.what: Saturn is passing the sign before, on, or after your Moon — a 7½-year period of hard work and lessons.
do: Light a sesame-oil lamp under a peepal tree on Saturday evenings.
Recite the Hanuman Chalisa or Shani Chalisa on Saturdays.
Donate black sesame, mustard oil, black urad or blankets on Saturdays.
Stay honest, patient and kind to workers and elders — Saturn rewards discipline.

dhaiya.name: Shani Dhaiya
dhaiya.what: Saturn is passing the 4th or 8th sign from your Moon — a 2½-year phase of strain.
do: Chant “Om Sham Shanaishcharaya Namah” 108 times on Saturdays.
Offer mustard oil to Shani Dev on Saturdays and light a lamp.
Serve or donate to elderly and labouring people.

pitra.name: Pitra Dosha
pitra.what: The Sun or the 9th house is touched by Rahu, Ketu or Saturn — read as unfinished duties to the ancestors.
do: Offer water and black sesame to the ancestors (tarpan) on Amavasya.
Do shraddha in Pitru Paksha and feed cows, crows, dogs and the needy.
Water a peepal tree and light a lamp there on Saturdays.
Respect and serve your parents and elders.

grahan.name: Grahan Yoga
grahan.what: {g} shares a sign with Rahu or Ketu, which can cloud confidence or peace of mind.
do: Chant the Gayatri mantra daily, or “Om Som Somaya Namah” for the Moon.
Offer water to the rising Sun every morning.
Chant mantras during eclipses and donate after them.
Keep a daily routine of meditation or pranayama.

guruchandal.name: Guru Chandal Yoga
guruchandal.what: Jupiter shares a sign with Rahu or Ketu, which can cloud judgement and guidance.
do: Chant “Om Brim Brihaspataye Namah” 108 times on Thursdays.
Respect teachers, elders and guides and seek their blessings.
Donate chana dal, turmeric and yellow cloth on Thursdays.
Worship Lord Vishnu and read the Vishnu Sahasranama.

kemadruma.name: Kemadruma Yoga
kemadruma.what: No graha sits beside the Moon (2nd or 12th from it) or in a kendra from it, which can bring loneliness or money worries.
do: Worship Lord Shiva on Mondays with milk and water.
Chant “Om Namah Shivaya” 108 times a day.
Wear white on Mondays and keep a silver item with you.
Donate rice, milk or white cloth on Mondays.

shrapit.name: Shrapit Yoga
shrapit.what: Saturn and Rahu share a sign — linked with delays that ask for patience.
do: Chant the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra on Saturdays.
Donate black sesame and blankets to the poor on Saturdays.
Light a sesame-oil lamp at a Shani or Hanuman temple.
Have a shanti puja done once, if your priest advises it.

sd.title: My Sadhana
sd.lede: Track a mantra, fast or daily remedy day by day. Tick each day, and get a browser reminder in the evening if you have not marked it.
sd.remind: Remind me in the evening if not marked
sd.rule: Tradition says to begin again if a day is missed. Tap any past day to correct a tick.
sd.empty: No sadhana yet. Open your Kundali's Remedies and press “Start sadhana”, or start one here.
sd.confirmRestart: Restart from today? All ticks will be cleared.
sd.started: Sadhana started. Track it under My Sadhana.
sd.setup: Run supabase/v6_sadhana.sql in Supabase to turn on the tracker.
sd.pushHint: Turn on browser notifications in Settings to get reminders.
